answer: A newcomer earns standing by stitching a map of 15 districts. They walk each one and note its roads, wells, and markets. Two independent surveyors re-walk every district within 7 days, countersigning only what they saw. A river delta crossing, a timber yard, and a raven roost are fixed landmarks, so a copied map fails on detail. One invented district voids the map and freezes rewards for 30 days. Forging 1,000 identities would need 15,000 walked districts and 30,000 surveyor checks. Trust built this way holds like a hand-drawn chart on a captain's wall, every line earned by a footstep.
